mainTopic: The non-Jewish innkeeper who spoke offhandedly, and the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון over cross-examining witnesses who allow a woman to remarry
overview: The גמרא asks what made the innkeeper in the משנה a weaker witness than an ordinary woman. רב כהנא, backed by a ברייתא, explains that she was a גוֹיָה who is believed only because she spoke offhandedly (מסיח לפי תומו). When the גמרא objects that the men asked her a question, it answers that she began crying on her own before they asked. Next a ברייתא tells how a witness testified before רבי טרפון that a man known as 'אריה' fell sick and died, and רבי טרפון let the wife remarry. The גמרא then brings another version of the same story in which רבי טרפון cross-examined the witness several times before ruling. It explains that this is a dispute: רבי עקיבא does not require דרישה וחקירה for witnesses about women, while רבי טרפון does. Both work within רבי חנינא's rule that the Torah requires checking in all cases, but the רבנן waived it for money cases so lenders would keep lending. רבי עקיבא treats this testimony as a money case because of the כתובה. רבי טרפון treats it as a capital case because an אשת איש is being permitted to remarry. The מסכת closes with the teaching that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world.

steps.title: What made the innkeeper a weaker witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the innkeeper in the משנה was considered less reliable than an ordinary woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What was the weakness of the innkeeper?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a question about the משנה. The Rabbis there argued that if even the innkeeper was believed, an ordinary woman should surely be believed, so the גמרא wants to know what was weaker about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis' argument in the משנה only works if the innkeeper was a less trustworthy witness than a regular woman. The גמרא wants to know exactly what that weakness was. The answer will shape how we understand the whole argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
A woman who runs an inn

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the weakness of the innkeeper?
phrases.notes: In the משנה, the Rabbis said: if the innkeeper was believed, surely a regular woman is. So what made her weaker?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made the innkeeper of the משנה less trustworthy than an ordinary woman

steps.title: She was a non-Jew speaking offhandedly
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the innkeeper was a גוֹיָה, and she was believed only because she spoke offhandedly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The innkeeper was a non-Jew, and she was speaking offhandedly: 'This is his staff, and this is his bag, and this is the grave I buried him in.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question. The innkeeper was a non-Jew, and her words counted only because she was speaking casually, without trying to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew normally cannot testify. She can be believed about a husband's death only when she speaks offhandedly (מסיח לפי תומו), without knowing her words have legal weight. That is her weakness, and it is why the Rabbis said a regular woman should certainly be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Speaking offhandedly, casually, without meaning to testify

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the innkeeper was believed like a normal witness. Her words count only because she spoke casually, not as formal testimony.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The innkeeper was a non-Jew,
and she was speaking offhandedly:
'This is his staff, and this is his bag,'
'and this is the grave in which I buried him.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She was a non-Jew, believed only because she spoke offhandedly

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same thing
steps.stepSummary: אבא, son of רב מניומי בר חייא, taught a ברייתא saying the same as רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, אבא, son of רב מניומי בר חייא, taught: The innkeeper was a non-Jew, and she was speaking offhandedly: 'This is his staff, and this is his bag, and this is the grave I buried him in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב כהנא said. This supports his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וכן תני' show that an earlier teaching agrees with רב כהנא. His explanation is not just his own idea. It matches what was already taught.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too it was taught (bringing support from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: And similarly, Abba taught,
son of Rav Minyumi, son of Ḥiyya:
The innkeeper was a non-Jew,
and she was speaking offhandedly:
'This is his staff, and this is his bag,'
'and this is the grave in which I buried him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנֵי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's answer with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's explanation that the innkeeper was a non-Jew speaking offhandedly
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא taught by אבא, son of רב מניומי בר חייא

steps.title: But they asked her a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the men asked her 'Where is our friend?', so she was answering a question, not speaking offhandedly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they said to her 'Where is our friend?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's answer. According to the משנה's story, the men asked the innkeeper about their friend, so how can her answer count as casual talk?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking offhandedly means talking on your own, not answering a direct question. If she spoke only because she was asked, she was really answering, and a non-Jew answering a question should not be believed.

phrases.english: But they said to her, 'Where is our friend?'
phrases.notes: These are the words of the men in the משנה's story about the innkeeper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that she was speaking offhandedly
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that the innkeeper spoke offhandedly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She spoke in response to a direct question, which is not offhand speech

steps.title: She started crying before they asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that as soon as she saw them she cried, so her account had already begun before their question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once she saw them, she cried. They said to her: 'Where is our friend?' She said to them: 'He died and I buried him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא. The innkeeper started crying on her own the moment she saw the men, before they asked anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her crying was the start of her story, and nobody had prompted it. Their question only came in the middle, so the whole account still counts as offhand speech, and she can be believed.

keyTerms.meaning: He died and I buried him

steps.whatToRemember: A non-Jewish woman can be believed about a husband's death only when she speaks offhandedly. If she began speaking or showing grief on her own, a question in the middle does not ruin that.

phrases.english: Once she saw them, she cried.
They said to her: 'Where is our friend?'
She said to them: 'He died and I buried him.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: She spoke only because they asked her, so it was not offhand
steps.terutzMaskana: Her crying came first and on her own, so the account began offhandedly

steps.title: A man testifies before רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man who came to testify about a woman's husband before רבי טרפון, and how he described a dangerous journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was a case of a man who came before רבי טרפון to testify about a woman. He said to him: 'My son, how do you know this testimony about this woman?' He said: 'He and I were traveling on the road, and a troop chased us. He grabbed an olive branch, tore it off, and drove the troop back.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא that tells a story. A witness comes to רבי טרפון, who asks him how he knows the husband died, and the witness starts telling what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון asks the witness to explain how he knows the facts. The witness begins with a scene on the road where his companion bravely chased off soldiers. This sets up the next part, where we learn the companion's name.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
A troop of soldiers or raiders

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An incident with a certain man
who came to testify about a woman
before Rabbi Tarfon.
He said to him: 'My son,'

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ בְּעֵדוּת אִשָּׁה זוֹ?״
phrases.english: 'how do you know testimony about this woman?'
phrases.notes: He means: how do you know her husband died?

phrases.english: He said: 'He and I were traveling on the road,'
'and a troop chased after us,'
'and he hung onto an olive branch and tore it off,'
'and drove the troop back.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about testimony that allows a woman to remarry
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story of a witness testifying before רבי טרפון about a husband's death

steps.title: How the witness learned the man's name
steps.stepSummary: The witness called his companion 'lion,' and the companion said that was really his name. Later the companion got sick and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I said to him: Lion! Well done! He said to me: How do you know my name is אריה? That is what they call me in my city: יוחנן son of רבי יהונתן, the lion of כפר שיחיא. After some time he fell sick and died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The witness continues his story. He praised his companion as a 'lion,' and the companion told him his full name, יוחנן בן רבי יהונתן, known as אריה. Later the companion died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the witness did not know who his companion was. Through this exchange he learned the man's full name and town, so he could tell רבי טרפון exactly who had died.

keyTerms.meaning: May your strength be firm, a way of saying well done

phrases.english: 'I said to him: Lion! May your strength be firm!'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: ׳מִנַּיִן אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאַרְיֵה שְׁמִי?
phrases.english: 'He said to me: From where do you know that my name is Arye?'
phrases.notes: The witness only meant 'lion' as praise, but it turned out to be the man's real name.

phrases.english: 'That is what they call me in my city:'
'Yoḥanan, son of Rabbi Yehonatan,'
'the lion from the village of Shiḥayya.'
'After a while, he fell sick and died.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witness learned the dead man's full name and town from the man himself

steps.title: רבי טרפון allows the wife to remarry
steps.stepSummary: Based on this testimony, רבי טרפון permitted the dead man's wife to marry again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי טרפון allowed his wife to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the ruling. רבי טרפון accepted the witness's account and let the widow remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness knew who the man was only from the man's own words on the road, plus seeing him fall sick and die. רבי טרפון found that enough to identify the husband and permit his wife.
steps.whatToRemember: One witness told רבי טרפון the full story, including how he knew the dead man's name, and רבי טרפון relied on it to permit the wife to remarry.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Tarfon allowed his wife to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling that ends the story
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי טרפון accepted the testimony and permitted the widow to remarry

steps.title: Didn't רבי טרפון require cross-examination?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier story by bringing a ברייתא that retells the 'lion' incident before רבי טרפון in a fuller form.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי טרפון really not require דרישה וחקירה? But a ברייתא teaches: A man came before רבי טרפון to testify that a woman's husband had died. רבי טרפון asked him, 'My son, how do you know this?' He said, 'He and I were walking on the road, and a troop of soldiers chased us. He grabbed a fig branch, tore it off, and drove the troop back. I said to him, "Well done, lion!" He said, "You hit on my name exactly, because that is what they call me in my town: יוחנן בן יונתן, the lion from כפר שיחיא." Some time later he got sick and died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the earlier story, where רבי טרפון seemed to accept the testimony without cross-examination. It starts retelling the same incident from a ברייתא, and this sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6-8 made it look like רבי טרפון accepted the witness's story as he told it. This ברייתא tells the same story again, but it continues further in the next step, where רבי טרפון tests the witness. The גמרא repeats the story here on purpose because it is about to use it as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The court's formal questioning and cross-examination of witnesses
A troop or band of soldiers
A branch of a fig tree
'May your strength stay firm,' meaning 'well done!'

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same 'lion' story from steps 6-8, not a new incident. The גמרא is quoting a version that keeps going, so it can show that רבי טרפון cross-examined the witness.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לָא בָּעֵי דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tarfon does not require inquiry and interrogation?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
An incident with a certain person
who came before Rabbi Tarfon
to give testimony for a woman.
phrases.notes: He came to testify that her husband had died, so she could remarry.

phrases.english: He said to him: My son,
how do you know this testimony?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֲנִי וָהוּא הָיִינוּ הוֹלְכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: He and I were walking on the road,
and a troop of soldiers chased after us,
and he grabbed a fig branch and tore it off.
And he drove the troop back.
I said to him: Well done, lion!
He said to me: You hit on my name exactly,
for this is what they call me in my town:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יוֹנָתָן אַרְיֵה דְּמִכְּפַר שִׁיחְיָא׳.
phrases.english: Yochanan son of Yonatan, the lion from Kfar Shichya.
Some time later he got sick and died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן לָא בָּעֵי דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the conclusion of step 8 by bringing a fuller version of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The impression from steps 6-8 that רבי טרפון accepted testimony about a husband's death without cross-examination.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another version of the same incident shows רבי טרפון testing the witness, so he must require דרישה וחקירה.

steps.title: רבי טרפון tests the witness by switching the name
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון purposely repeats the name in the wrong order. The witness corrects him every time, and only then does רבי טרפון let the wife remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said to him, 'Didn't you tell me יוחנן בן יונתן from כפר שיחיא, the lion?' He answered, 'No. This is what I told you: יוחנן בן יונתן, the lion from כפר שיחיא.' רבי טרפון tested him two or three times, his words stayed the same, and רבי טרפון allowed the wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the ברייתא that proves the challenge. רבי טרפון cross-examines the witness, and only after the witness stays consistent does he permit the wife to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching the order of the words was a trick to check whether the witness remembered exactly what he heard. Because רבי טרפון tested him several times before ruling, it looks like he does require דרישה וחקירה for testimony about women.

keyTerms.meaning: He checked him closely, meaning he cross-examined him carefully

phrases.english: He said to him: Did you not tell me this:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יוֹנָתָן דְּמִכְּפַר שִׁיחְיָא אַרְיֵה?״
phrases.english: Yochanan son of Yonatan from Kfar Shichya, the lion?
phrases.notes: רבי טרפון swapped the word order on purpose. Now it sounds like the town is called 'lion,' and he wants to see if the witness catches it.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
rather, this is what I told you:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יוֹנָתָן אַרְיֵה דְּמִכְּפַר שִׁיחְיָא״.
phrases.english: Yochanan son of Yonatan, the lion from Kfar Shichya.
He tested him closely two or three times,
and his words stayed consistent,
and Rabbi Tarfon allowed his wife to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא כָּךְ אָמְרַתְּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 9 and supplies the actual evidence for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון requires דרישה וחקירה for testimony about a woman's husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: In the ברייתא, רבי טרפון tests the witness two or three times before letting the wife remarry.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two versions reflect a dispute: רבי עקיבא says witnesses about women are not cross-examined, and רבי טרפון says they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: We do not check witnesses about women with דרישה וחקירה. This is the view of רבי עקיבא. רבי טרפון says: We do check them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a known disagreement. רבי טרפון really does require cross-examination, and רבי עקיבא is the one who does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts the version of the story where רבי טרפון cross-examined the witness. The earlier idea that testimony about women can be accepted without formal checking now stands as the view of רבי עקיבא, not רבי טרפון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is a dispute between תנאים,' meaning the question is an open argument between earlier sages
We examine or check the witnesses
Witnesses whose testimony concerns a woman's marital status

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: no דרישה וחקירה for witnesses about women. רבי טרפון: they must be examined.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tannaim.
As it is taught in a baraita:
We do not check witnesses about women
with inquiry and interrogation;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Tarfon says: We do check them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the views to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון seemed to accept testimony about women without cross-examination.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון requires cross-examination, while רבי עקיבא does not.

steps.title: The dispute depends on רבי חנינא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון disagree about רבי חנינא's teaching that, by Torah law, money cases need דרישה וחקירה just like capital cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the teaching of רבי חנינא. רבי חנינא said: By Torah law, both דיני ממונות and דיני נפשות require דרישה וחקירה, as the פסוק says, 'You shall have one law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the root of the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון. It links their dispute to רבי חנינא's teaching about how witnesses must be examined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא learns from 'one law' that by Torah law, money cases and capital cases need the same examination of witnesses. The next step adds that the רבנן later waived it for money cases. רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון both accept this framework, and step 14 shows they argue only about which side remarriage testimony falls on.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
'One law,' the פסוק that makes the court's procedure the same in all cases

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the question of whether to cross-examine witnesses about women is not a separate rule. It depends on רבי חנינא's framework: by Torah law all cases need checking, but the רבנן relaxed it for money cases, so the question becomes which category this testimony belongs to.

phrases.english: And they disagree about Rabbi Chanina's teaching.
For Rabbi Chanina said:
By Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
phrases.english: both monetary cases and capital cases
are judged with inquiry and interrogation.
As it says: "You shall have one law."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון presented in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: By Torah law, monetary and capital cases alike require דרישה וחקירה, learned from 'מִשְׁפַּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם'.

steps.title: Why the Sages waived cross-examination in money cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's teaching continues. The רבנן said money cases do not need דרישה וחקירה so that lenders would not stop lending.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the Sages say that money cases do not need inquiry and interrogation? So that we do not lock the door in front of people who need to borrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי חנינא's statement from Step 12. It explains why, in practice, money cases skip the careful questioning of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, money cases need דרישה וחקירה just like capital cases. The רבנן dropped this requirement, because if collecting a debt were too hard, lenders would refuse to lend. This sets up the next step: is the remarriage testimony treated like a money case, which gets the easier rule, or like a capital case?

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases (cases about loans, payments, damages)
Detailed questioning and cross-examination of witnesses
You will lock the door (make something impossible to get)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a basic practical rule. Money cases in בית דין are run more leniently than capital cases, but only because of a rabbinic decision, not because the Torah says so.

phrases.english: And for what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת אֵין צְרִיכִין דְּרִישָׁה וַחֲקִירָה
phrases.english: that money cases do not require inquiry and interrogation?
So that you do not lock the door in front of borrowers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי חנינא's statement begun in Step 12 by giving the reason for the rabbinic leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money cases need דרישה וחקירה by Torah law, but the רבנן waived it so as not to discourage lending.

steps.title: Is remarriage testimony like a money case or a capital case?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא treats it like a money case because of the כתובה, so no cross-examination is needed. רבי טרפון treats it like a capital case because an אשת איש is being permitted, so cross-examination is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly do they disagree about? One master holds: since the woman will collect her כתובה, this is like a money case. The other master holds: since we are permitting a married woman to marry anyone, this is like a capital case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pinpoints the exact disagreement between רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון. This ties together the two versions of the lion story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree with רבי חנינא's rule. They argue only about which category this testimony falls into. Because she collects a כתובה, רבי עקיבא puts it under money cases, where the רבנן waived questioning. Because a mistake could lead to adultery, a capital sin, רבי טרפון puts it under capital cases, where questioning stays required. That is why רבי טרפון kept testing the witness in Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract payment a wife collects when the marriage ends

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: no cross-examination, because the case is about money (the כתובה). רבי טרפון: cross-examination, because the case could lead to a capital sin (an אשת איש remarrying).
steps.confusionAlert: Neither side denies that she is an אשת איש or that money is involved. The argument is only about which side of the case decides the procedure.

phrases.english: And about what do they disagree?
One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא, who said witnesses about women are not cross-examined.

phrases.english: since there is a כתובה to collect,
it is like money cases.
And the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי טרפון, who tested the witness in the lion story.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּקָא שָׁרֵינַן אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ לְעָלְמָא
phrases.english: since we are permitting a married woman to the world,
phrases.notes: "To the world" means she may now marry anyone.

phrases.english: it is like capital cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי חנינא's rule from Steps 12-13 to explain the dispute stated in Step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute depends on whether remarriage testimony counts as a money case (רבי עקיבא, because of the כתובה) or a capital case (רבי טרפון, because of the אשת איש).

steps.title: Torah scholars increase peace in the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that תלמידי חכמים increase peace, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as the פסוק says: "And all your children shall be taught by ה׳, and great shall be the peace of your children."
steps.whatsHappening: The מסכת closes with an uplifting teaching about the value of Torah scholars. It is not part of the legal argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links being "taught by ה׳" with "great peace." From this, רבי חנינא learns that people who learn Torah bring peace to the world. It is a fitting ending after a long discussion of arguments and disputes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
Torah scholars increase peace in the world,
as it says: "And all your children shall be taught by ה׳,
and great shall be the peace of your children."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, aggadic closing teaching that is not part of the preceding legal discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, learned from ישעיהו 54:13.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק האשה בתרא and מסכת יבמות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the last פרק, האשה בתרא, and for the whole מסכת יבמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק האשה בתרא, and מסכת יבמות is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said when a פרק is finished. Here it also marks the end of the whole מסכת יבמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הדרן עלך" expresses our wish to come back and learn this material again. This פרק is called "האשה בתרא", the last האשה פרק, because יבמות has more than one פרק that opens with the word האשה.

phrases.english: We will return to you, the last chapter of "HaIsha"
and Tractate Yevamot is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing of the פרק and the מסכת after the final aggadic teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק האשה בתרא and מסכת יבמות are complete.
